sEn: Hindsight Experience Replay enables sample-efficient learning from sparse, binary rewards, eliminating the need for reward engineering.
sZh: 后见经验回放实现了从稀疏二元奖励中的样本高效学习，无需进行奖励工程。
absEn: Dealing with sparse rewards is one of the biggest challenges in Reinforcement Learning (RL). We present a novel technique called Hindsight Experience Replay which allows sample-efficient learning from rewards which are sparse and binary and therefore avoid the need for complicated reward engineering. It can be combined with an arbitrary off-policy RL algorithm and may be seen as a form of implicit curriculum. We demonstrate our approach on the task of manipulating objects with a robotic arm. In particular, we run experiments on three different tasks: pushing, sliding, and pick-and-place, in each case using only binary rewards indicating whether or not the task is completed. Our ablation studies show that Hindsight Experience Replay is a crucial ingredient which makes training possible in these challenging environments. We show that our policies trained on a physics simulation can be deployed on a physical robot and successfully complete the task.
absZh: 处理稀疏奖励是强化学习（RL）中最大的挑战之一。我们提出了一种称为事后经验回放（Hindsight Experience Replay）的新技术，该技术允许从稀疏且二元的奖励中进行样本高效学习，从而避免了对复杂奖励工程的需求。它可以与任意离策略RL算法结合，并可被视为一种隐式课程学习形式。我们在用机械臂操作物体的任务上展示了我们的方法。具体来说，我们在三个不同的任务上进行了实验：推动、滑动和抓取放置，每种情况下仅使用指示任务是否完成的二元奖励。我们的消融研究表明，事后经验回放是使得在这些具有挑战性的环境中能够进行训练的关键因素。我们展示了在物理仿真中训练的策略可以部署到实体机器人上并成功完成任务。

paras.en: Abstract Dealing with sparse rewards is one of the biggest challenges in Reinforcement Learning (RL). We present a novel technique called Hindsight Experience Replay which allows sample-efficient learning from rewards which are sparse and binary and therefore avoid the need for complicated reward engineering. It can be combined with an arbitrary off-policy RL algorithm and may be seen as a form of implicit curriculum. We demonstrate our approach on the task of manipulating objects with a robotic arm. In particular, we run experiments on three different tasks: pushing, sliding, and pick-and-place, in each case using only binary rewards indicating whether or not the task is completed. Our ablation studies show that Hindsight Experience Replay is a crucial ingredient which makes training possible in these challenging environments. We show that our policies trained on a physics simulation can be deployed on a physical robot and successfully complete the task. paras.en: Reinforcement learning (RL) combined with neural networks has recently led to a wide range of successes in learning policies for sequential decision-making problems. This includes simulated environments, such as playing Atari games (Mnih et al., 2015), and defeating the best human player at the game of Go (Silver et al., 2016), as well as robotic tasks such as helicopter control (Ng et al., 2006), hitting a baseball (Peters and Schaal, 2008), screwing a cap onto a bottle (Levine et al., 2015), or door opening (Chebotar et al., 2016). However, a common challenge, especially for robotics, is the need to engineer a reward function that not only reflects the task at hand but is also carefully shaped (Ng et al., 1999) to guide the policy optimization. For example, Popov et al. (2017) use a cost function consisting of five relatively complicated terms which need to be carefully weighted in order to train a policy for stacking a brick on top of another one. The necessity of cost engineering limits the applicability of RL in the real world because it requires both RL expertise and domain-specific knowledge. Moreover, it is not applicable in situations where we do not know what admissible behaviour may look like. It is therefore of great practical relevance to develop algorithms which can learn from unshaped reward signals, e.g. a binary signal indicating successful task completion. One ability humans have, unlike the current generation of model-free RL algorithms, is to learn almost as much from achieving an undesired outcome as from the desired one. Imagine that you are learning how to play hockey and are trying to shoot a puck into a net. You hit the puck but it misses the net on the right side. It is however possible to draw another conclusion, namely that this sequence of actions would be successful if the net had been placed further to the right. In this paper we introduce a technique called Hindsight Experience Replay (HER) which allows the algorithm to perform exactly this kind of reasoning and can be combined with any off-policy RL algorithm. It is applicable whenever there are multiple goals which can be achieved, e.g. achieving each state of the system may be treated as a separate goal. Not only does HER improve the sample efficiency in this setting, but more importantly, it makes learning possible even if the reward signal is sparse and binary. Our approach is based on training universal policies (Schaul et al., 2015a) which take as input not only the current state, but also a goal state. The pivotal idea behind HER is to replay each episode with a different goal than the one the agent was trying to achieve, e.g. one of the goals which was achieved in the episode.

paras.en: In this section, we introduce the reinforcement learning formalism used in the paper, as well as the RL algorithms we use in our experiments. 2.1
paras.zh: 在本节中，我们介绍了本文使用的强化学习形式化描述以及实验中使用的RL算法。2.1

paras.en: We consider the standard reinforcement learning formalism consisting of an agent interacting with an environment. To simplify the exposition, we assume that the environment is fully observable. An environment is described by a set of states S, a set of actions A, a distribution of initial states p(s0), a reward function r : S \times A \rightarrow \mathbb{R}, transition probabilities p(s_{t+1} | s_t, a_t), and a discount factor \gamma \in [0, 1]. A deterministic policy is a mapping from states to actions: \pi : S \rightarrow A. Every episode starts with sampling an initial state s0. At every timestep t, the agent produces an action based on the current state: a_t = \pi(s_t). Then it gets the reward r_t = r(s_t, a_t) and the environment's new state is sampled from the distribution p(\cdot | s_t, a_t). A discounted sum of future rewards is called a return: R_t = \sum_{i=t}^{\infty} \gamma^{i-t} r_i. The agent's goal is to maximize its expected return \mathbb{E}_{s_0}[R_0 | s_0]. The Q-function or action-value function is defined as Q^{\pi}(s_t, a_t) = \mathbb{E}[R_t | s_t, a_t].
paras.zh: 我们考虑标准的强化学习形式化描述，包括一个与环境交互的智能体。为简化阐述，我们假设环境是完全可观察的。环境由一组状态S、一组动作A、初始状态分布p(s0)、奖励函数r: S × A → ℝ、转移概率p(s_{t+1} | s_t, a_t)以及折扣因子γ ∈ [0, 1]描述。确定性策略是从状态到动作的映射：π: S → A。每个回合从采样初始状态s0开始。在每个时间步t，智能体根据当前状态产生动作：a_t = π(s_t)。然后它获得奖励r_t = r(s_t, a_t)，并且环境的新状态从分布p(·|s_t, a_t)中采样。未来奖励的折扣和称为回报：R_t = ∑_{i=t}^{∞} γ^{i-t} r_i。智能体的目标是最大化其期望回报E_{s_0}[R_0 | s_0]。Q函数或动作值函数定义为Q^π(s_t, a_t) = E[R_t | s_t, a_t]。

paras.en:
Let \pi^* denote an optimal policy, i.e., any policy \pi^* such that Q^{\pi^*}(s, a) \geq Q^{\pi}(s, a) for every s \in S, a \in A and any policy \pi. All optimal policies have the same Q-function which is called the optimal Q-function and denoted Q^*. It is easy to show that it satisfies the following equation, called the Bellman equation:
\[ Q^*(s, a) = \mathbb{E}_{s' \sim p(\cdot | s, a)} \big[ r(s, a) + \gamma \max_{a' \in A} Q^*(s', a') \big]. \]
paras.zh:
令π*表示最优策略，即对于任意s∈S、a∈A和任意策略π，有Q^{π*}(s,a) ≥ Q^π(s,a)的策略。所有最优策略具有相同的Q函数，称为最优Q函数，记作Q*。容易证明它满足以下方程，称为Bellman方程：
\[ Q^*(s, a) = \mathbb{E}_{s' \sim p(\cdot | s, a)} \big[ r(s, a) + \gamma \max_{a' \in A} Q^*(s', a') \big]. \]

paras.en: Deep Q-Networks (DQN) (Mnih et al., 2015) is a model-free RL algorithm for discrete action spaces. Here we sketch it only informally; see Mnih et al. (2015) for more details. In DQN, we maintain a neural network Q which approximates Q^*. A greedy policy w.r.t. Q is defined as \pi_Q(s) = \argmax_{a \in A} Q(s, a). An \epsilon-greedy policy w.r.t. Q is a policy which with probability \epsilon takes a random action (sampled uniformly from A) and takes the action \pi_Q(s) with probability 1 - \epsilon.
paras.zh: 深度Q网络（DQN）（Mnih等，2015）是一种针对离散动作空间的无模型RL算法。这里我们仅非正式地概述，更多细节见Mnih等（2015）。在DQN中，我们维护一个神经网络Q来近似Q*。相对于Q的贪婪策略定义为π_Q(s) = argmax_{a∈A} Q(s, a)。相对于Q的ε-贪婪策略是一个以概率ε采取随机动作（从A中均匀采样）、以概率1-ε采取动作π_Q(s)的策略。

paras.en:
During training, we generate episodes using an \epsilon-greedy policy w.r.t. the current approximation of the action-value function Q. The transition tuples (s_t, a_t, r_t, s_{t+1}) encountered during training are stored in the so-called replay buffer. The generation of new episodes is interleaved with neural network training. The network is trained using mini-batch gradient descent on the loss L which encourages the approximated Q-function to satisfy the Bellman equation:
\[ L = \mathbb{E} \big[ (Q(s_t, a_t) - y_t)^2 \big], \]
where y_t = r_t + \gamma \max_{a' \in A} Q(s_{t+1}, a') and the tuples (s_t, a_t, r_t, s_{t+1}) are sampled from the replay buffer. In order to make this optimization procedure more stable, the targets y_t are usually computed using a separate target network which changes at a slower pace than the main network. A common practice 1
paras.zh:
在训练过程中，我们使用相对于当前动作值函数Q的ε-贪婪策略生成回合。训练中遇到的转换元组(s_t, a_t, r_t, s_{t+1})存储在所谓的经验回放缓冲区中。新回合的生成与神经网络训练交替进行。网络通过小批量梯度下降训练损失L，该损失鼓励近似的Q函数满足Bellman方程：
\[ L = \mathbb{E} \big[ (Q(s_t, a_t) - y_t)^2 \big], \]
其中 y_t = r_t + \gamma \max_{a' \in A} Q(s_{t+1}, a')，元组(s_t, a_t, r_t, s_{t+1})从经验回放缓冲区中采样。为了使优化过程更稳定，目标y_t通常使用一个单独的目标网络计算，该网络的变化速度比主网络慢。常见做法 1

paras.en: The targets $y_t$ depend on the network parameters but this dependency is ignored during backpropagation.
paras.zh: 目标值 $y_t$ 依赖于网络参数，但反向传播过程中忽略此依赖关系。

paras.en: One approach is to periodically set the weights of the target network to the current weights of the main network (e.g., Mnih et al., 2015) or to use a Polyak-averaged (Polyak and Juditsky, 1992) version of the main network instead (Lillicrap et al., 2015).
paras.zh: 一种方法是定期将目标网络的权重视为主网络当前的权重（例如 Mnih 等人，2015），或使用主网络的 Polyak 平均（Polyak 和 Juditsky，1992）版本代替（Lillicrap 等人，2015）。

paras.en: Deep Deterministic Policy Gradients (DDPG) (Lillicrap et al., 2015) is a model-free RL algorithm for continuous action spaces. Here we sketch it only informally, see Lillicrap et al. (2015) for more details. In DDPG we maintain two neural networks: a target policy (also called an actor) $\pi: S \to A$ and an action-value function approximator (called the critic) $Q: S \times A \to \mathbb{R}$. The critic's job is to approximate the actor's action-value function $Q^\pi$. Episodes are generated using a behavioral policy which is a noisy version of the target policy, e.g., $\pi_b(s) = \pi(s) + \mathcal{N}(0, 1)$. The critic is trained in a similar way as the Q-function in DQN but the targets $y_t$ are computed using actions outputted by the actor, i.e., $y_t = r_t + \gamma Q(s_{t+1}, \pi(s_{t+1}))$. The actor is trained with mini-batch gradient descent on the loss $L_a = -\mathbb{E}_s Q(s, \pi(s))$, where $s$ is sampled from the replay buffer. The gradient of $L_a$ w.r.t. actor parameters can be computed by backpropagation through the combined critic and actor networks.
paras.zh: 深度确定性策略梯度（DDPG）（Lillicrap 等人，2015）是一种用于连续动作空间的无模型强化学习算法。此处仅作非正式概述，详情参见 Lillicrap 等人（2015）。DDPG 维护两个神经网络：一个目标策略（也称为演员）$\pi: S \to A$ 和一个动作价值函数近似器（称为评论家）$Q: S \times A \to \mathbb{R}$。评论家的任务是近似演员的动作价值函数 $Q^\pi$。通过行为策略生成回合，该策略是目标策略的带噪版本，例如 $\pi_b(s) = \pi(s) + \mathcal{N}(0, 1)$。评论家的训练方式与 DQN 中的 Q 函数类似，但目标 $y_t$ 使用演员输出的动作计算，即 $y_t = r_t + \gamma Q(s_{t+1}, \pi(s_{t+1}))$。演员通过小批量梯度下降在损失 $L_a = -\mathbb{E}_s Q(s, \pi(s))$ 上训练，其中 $s$ 从经验回放缓冲区采样。$L_a$ 关于演员参数的梯度可通过联合的评论家和演员网络反向传播计算。

paras.en: Universal Value Function Approximators (UVFA) (Schaul et al., 2015a) is an extension of DQN to the setup where there is more than one goal we may try to achieve. Let $\mathcal{G}$ be the space of possible goals. Every goal $g \in \mathcal{G}$ corresponds to some reward function $r_g: S \times A \to \mathbb{R}$. Every episode starts with sampling a state-goal pair from some distribution $p(s_0, g)$. The goal stays fixed for the whole episode. At every timestep the agent gets as input not only the current state but also the current goal $\pi: S \times \mathcal{G} \to A$ and gets the reward $r_t = r_g(s_t, a_t)$. The Q-function now depends not only on a state-action pair but also on a goal $Q^\pi(s_t, a_t, g) = \mathbb{E}[R_t \mid s_t, a_t, g]$. Schaul et al. (2015a) show that in this setup it is possible to train an approximator to the Q-function using direct bootstrapping from the Bellman equation (just like in case of DQN) and that a greedy policy derived from it can generalize to previously unseen state-action pairs. The extension of this approach to DDPG is straightforward.
paras.zh: 通用价值函数近似器（UVFA）（Schaul 等人，2015a）是 DQN 在存在多个可能目标时的扩展。令 $\mathcal{G}$ 为可能目标的空间。每个目标 $g \in \mathcal{G}$ 对应某个奖励函数 $r_g: S \times A \to \mathbb{R}$。每个回合从某个分布 $p(s_0, g)$ 中采样一个状态-目标对开始。目标在整个回合中固定。在每个时间步，智能体不仅输入当前状态，还输入当前目标 $\pi: S \times \mathcal{G} \to A$，并获得奖励 $r_t = r_g(s_t, a_t)$。Q 函数现在不仅依赖于状态-动作对，还依赖于目标 $Q^\pi(s_t, a_t, g) = \mathbb{E}[R_t \mid s_t, a_t, g]$。Schaul 等人（2015a）表明，在此设置下，可以使用 Bellman 方程的直接自举（如同 DQN 的情况）训练 Q 函数的近似器，并且由此导出的贪心策略可以泛化到未见过的状态-动作对。将该方法扩展到 DDPG 是直接的。

paras.en: Consider a bit-flipping environment with the state space $S = \{0, 1\}^n$ and the action space $A = \{0, 1, \ldots, n-1\}$ for some integer $n$ in which executing the $i$-th action flips the $i$-th bit of the state. For every episode we sample uniformly an initial state as well as a target state and the policy gets a reward of $-1$ as long as it is not in the target state, i.e., $r_g(s, a) = -[s \neq g]$.
paras.zh: 考虑一个比特翻转环境，状态空间 $S = \{0, 1\}^n$，动作空间 $A = \{0, 1, \ldots, n-1\}$（其中 $n$ 为整数），执行第 $i$ 个动作会翻转状态的第 $i$ 位。对于每个回合，我们均匀采样初始状态和目标状态，当策略未达到目标状态时获得奖励 $-1$，即 $r_g(s, a) = -[s \neq g]$。

paras.en: Standard RL algorithms are bound to fail in this environment for n > 40 because they will never experience any reward other than −1. Figure 1: Bit-flipping experiment. Notice that using techniques for improving exploration (e.g., VIME (Houthooft et al., 2016), count-based exploration (Ostrovski et al., 2017), or bootstrapped DQN (Osband et al., 2016)) does not help DQN+HER here because the real problem is not in lack of diversity of states being visited, rather it is simply impractical to explore such a large state space. The standard solution to this problem would be to use a shaped reward function which is more informative and guides the agent towards the goal, e.g., \(r_g(s, a) = -\|s - g\|_2\). While using a shaped reward solves the problem in our toy environment, it may be difficult to apply to more complicated problems. We investigate the results of reward shaping experimentally in Sec. 4.4. Instead of shaping the reward we propose a different solution which does not require any domain knowledge. paras.en: A state sequence \(s_1, ..., s_T\) and a goal \(g \ne s_1, ..., s_T\) which implies that the agent received a reward of −1 at every timestep. The pivotal idea behind our approach is to re-examine this trajectory with a different goal — while this trajectory may not help us learn how to achieve the state \(g\), it definitely tells us something about how to achieve the state \(s_T\). This information can be harvested by using an off-policy RL algorithm and experience replay where we replace \(g\) in the replay buffer by \(s_T\). In addition we can still replay with the original goal \(g\) left intact in the replay buffer. With this modification at least half of the replayed trajectories contain rewards different from −1 and learning becomes much simpler. Fig. 1 compares the final performance of DQN with and without this additional replay technique which we call Hindsight Experience Replay (HER). DQN without HER can only solve the task for \(n \le 13\) while DQN with HER easily solves the task for \(n\) up to 50. See Appendix A for the details of the experimental setup. Note that this approach combined with powerful function approximators (e.g., deep neural networks) allows the agent to learn how to achieve the goal \(g\) even if it has never observed it during training. We more formally describe our approach in the following sections. 3.2
paras.zh: 一个状态序列\(s_1, ..., s_T\)和一个目标\(g \ne s_1, ..., s_T\)，这意味着智能体在每个时间步都收到-1的奖励。我们方法的关键思想是用不同的目标重新审视这个轨迹——虽然这个轨迹可能无助于学习如何达到状态\(g\)，但它无疑告诉我们如何达到状态\(s_T\)。通过使用离策略RL算法和经验回放，我们可以利用这些信息，将回放缓冲区中的\(g\)替换为\(s_T\)。此外，我们还可以保留原始目标\(g\)不变进行回放。通过这种修改，至少一半的回放轨迹包含不同于-1的奖励，学习变得简单得多。图1比较了有和没有这种额外回放技术（我们称之为事后经验回放（Hindsight Experience Replay, HER））的DQN的最终性能。没有HER的DQN只能解决\(n \le 13\)的任务，而带有HER的DQN可以轻松解决\(n\)高达50的任务。实验设置的细节见附录A。注意，这种方法结合强大的函数逼近器（例如深度神经网络）使智能体能够学习如何达到目标\(g\)，即使它在训练中从未观察到该目标。我们在后续章节中更正式地描述我们的方法。3.2

paras.en: We are interested in training agents which learn to achieve multiple different goals. We follow the approach from Universal Value Function Approximators (Schaul et al., 2015a), i.e., we train policies and value functions which take as input not only a state \(s \in S\) but also a goal \(g \in G\). Moreover, we show that training an agent to perform multiple tasks can be easier than training it to perform only one task (see Sec. 4.3 for details) and therefore our approach may be applicable even if there is only one task we would like the agent to perform (a similar situation was recently observed by Pinto and Gupta (2016)). We assume that every goal \(g \in G\) corresponds to some predicate \(f_g: S \to {0, 1}\) and that the agent's goal is to achieve any state \(s\) that satisfies \(f_g(s) = 1\). In the case when we want to exactly specify the desired state of the system we may use \(S = G\) and \(f_g(s) = [s = g]\). The goals can also specify only some properties of the state, e.g., suppose that \(S = \mathbb{R}^2\) and we want to be able to achieve an arbitrary state with the given value of \(x\) coordinate. In this case \(G = \mathbb{R}\) and \(f_g((x, y)) = [x = g]\).
paras.zh: 我们感兴趣的是训练学习实现多个不同目标的智能体。我们遵循通用价值函数逼近器（Schaul等人，2015a）的方法，即训练策略和价值函数，其输入不仅包括状态\(s \in S\)，还包括目标\(g \in G\)。此外，我们证明了训练智能体执行多个任务比训练其只执行一个任务更容易（详见第4.3节），因此我们的方法即使只有一项任务也可能适用（类似情况最近由Pinto和Gupta（2016）观察到）。我们假设每个目标\(g \in G\)对应某个谓词\(f_g: S \to {0, 1}\)，并且智能体的目标是达到任何满足\(f_g(s)=1\)的状态\(s\)。当我们想精确指定系统的期望状态时，可以使用\(S = G\)和\(f_g(s) = [s = g]\)。目标也可以只指定状态的某些属性，例如，假设\(S = \mathbb{R}^2\)，我们希望能够达到x坐标为给定值的任意状态。在这种情况下，\(G = \mathbb{R}\)且\(f_g((x, y)) = [x = g]\)。

paras.en: Moreover, we assume that given a state \(s\) we can easily find a goal \(g\) which is satisfied in this state. More formally, we assume that there is given a mapping \(m: S \to G\) s.t. \(\forall s \in S\) \(f_{m(s)}(s) = 1\). Notice that this assumption is not very restrictive and can usually be satisfied. In the case where each goal corresponds to a state we want to achieve, i.e., \(G = S\) and \(f_g(s) = [s = g]\), the mapping \(m\) is just an identity. For the case of 2-dimensional state and 1-dimensional goals from the previous paragraph this mapping is also very simple: \(m((x, y)) = x\).
paras.zh: 此外，我们假设给定一个状态\(s\)，我们可以很容易地找到一个在该状态下满足的目标\(g\)。更正式地说，我们假设存在一个映射\(m: S \to G\)，使得\(\forall s \in S\) \(f_{m(s)}(s)=1\)。注意，这个假设并不是非常严格，通常都可以满足。在每个目标对应一个我们想要达到的状态的情况下，即\(G = S\)且\(f_g(s) = [s = g]\)，映射\(m\)就是恒等映射。对于上一段中2维状态和1维目标的情况，这个映射也非常简单：\(m((x, y)) = x\)。

paras.en: A universal policy can be trained using an arbitrary RL algorithm by sampling goals and initial states from some distributions, running the agent for some number of timesteps and giving it a negative reward at every timestep when the goal is not achieved, i.e., \(r_g(s, a) = -[f_g(s) = 0]\). This does not however work very well in practice because this reward function is sparse and not very informative. In order to solve this problem we introduce the technique of Hindsight Experience Replay which is the crux of our approach.
paras.zh: 通过从某些分布中采样目标和初始状态，运行智能体若干时间步，并在每个时间步当目标未达成时给予负奖励，即 \(r_g(s, a) = -[f_g(s)=0]\)，可以使用任意RL算法训练通用策略。然而，这种方法在实践中效果不佳，因为该奖励函数稀疏且信息量不足。为解决此问题，我们引入了后见经验回放（Hindsight Experience Replay）技术，这是本文方法的核心。

paras.en: The idea behind Hindsight Experience Replay (HER) is very simple: after experiencing some episode \(s_0, s_1, \dots, s_T\) we store in the replay buffer every transition \(s_t \to s_{t+1}\) not only with the original goal used for this episode but also with a subset of other goals. Notice that the goal being pursued influences the agent's actions but not the environment dynamics and therefore we can replay each trajectory with an arbitrary goal assuming that we use an off-policy RL algorithm like DQN (Mnih et al., 2015), DDPG (Lillicrap et al., 2015), NAF (Gu et al., 2016) or SDQN (Metz et al., 2017). One choice which has to be made in order to use HER is the set of additional goals used for replay. In the simplest version of our algorithm we replay each trajectory with the goal \(m(s_T)\), i.e., the goal which is achieved in the final state of the episode. We experimentally compare different types and quantities of additional goals for replay in Sec. 4.5. In all cases we also replay each trajectory with the original goal pursued in the episode. See Alg. 1 for a more formal description of the algorithm.
paras.zh: 后见经验回放（HER）的思路非常简单：在经历某个回合 \(s_0, s_1, \dots, s_T\) 后，我们将每个转移 \(s_t \to s_{t+1}\) 存入回放缓冲区时，不仅使用该回合的原始目标，还使用其他目标的一个子集。注意到，追求的目标影响智能体的动作但不影响环境动态，因此我们可以假设使用离策略RL算法（如DQN（Mnih等人，2015）、DDPG（Lillicrap等人，2015）、NAF（Gu等人，2016）或SDQN（Metz等人，2017））的情况下，用任意目标重放每条轨迹。使用HER时需要做出的一个选择是用于回放的额外目标集。在我们算法的最简单版本中，我们使用目标 \(m(s_T)\) 重放每条轨迹，即在该回合最终状态达成的目标。我们在第4.5节实验比较了不同种类和数量的额外目标用于回放。在所有情况下，我们也使用该回合追求的原始目标重放每条轨迹。算法1给出了更形式化的算法描述。

paras.en:
Algorithm 1 Hindsight Experience Replay (HER)
Given:
• an off-policy RL algorithm \(\mathcal{A}\), e.g., DQN, DDPG, NAF, SDQN
• a strategy \(\mathcal{S}\) for sampling goals for replay, e.g., \(\mathcal{S}(s_0,\dots,s_T) = m(s_T)\)
• a reward function \(r: S \times A \times G \to \mathbb{R}\), e.g., \(r(s,a,g) = -[f_g(s)=0]\)
Initialize \(\mathcal{A}\) (e.g., initialize neural networks)
Initialize replay buffer \(\mathcal{R}\)
for episode = 1, M do
  Sample a goal \(g\) and an initial state \(s_0\).
  for t = 0, T-1 do
    Sample an action \(a_t\) using the behavioral policy from \(\mathcal{A}\): \(a_t \leftarrow \pi_b(s_t || g)\) (|| denotes concatenation)
    Execute the action \(a_t\) and observe a new state \(s_{t+1}\)
  end for
  for t = 0, T-1 do
    \(r_t := r(s_t, a_t, g)\)
    Store the transition \(s_t||g, a_t, r_t, s_{t+1}||g)\ in \(\mathcal{R}\) (standard experience replay)
    Sample a set of additional goals for replay \(\mathcal{G} := \mathcal{S}(\text{current episode})\)
    for \(g' \in \mathcal{G}\) do
      \(r' := r(s_t, a_t, g')\)
      Store the transition \(s_t||g', a_t, r', s_{t+1}||g')\ in \(\mathcal{R}\) (HER)
    end for
  end for
  for t = 1, N do
    Sample a minibatch \(\mathcal{B}\) from the replay buffer \(\mathcal{R}\)
    Perform one step of optimization using \(\mathcal{A}\) and minibatch \(\mathcal{B}\)
  end for
end for
HER may be seen as a form of implicit curriculum as the goals used for replay naturally shift from ones which are simple to achieve even by a random agent to more difficult ones. However, in contrast to explicit curriculum, HER does not require having any control over the distribution of initial environment states. Not only does HER learn with extremely sparse rewards, in our experiments it also performs better with sparse rewards than with shaped ones (See Sec. 4.4). These results are indicative of the practical challenges with reward shaping, and that shaped rewards would often constitute a compromise on the metric we truly care about (such as binary success/failure).
paras.zh:
算法1 后见经验回放（HER）
给定：
• 一个离策略RL算法 \(\mathcal{A}\)，例如DQN、DDPG、NAF、SDQN
• 一个用于回放的目标采样策略 \(\mathcal{S}\)，例如 \(\mathcal{S}(s_0,\dots,s_T) = m(s_T)\)
• 一个奖励函数 \(r: S \times A \times G \to \mathbb{R}\)，例如 \(r(s,a,g) = -[f_g(s)=0]\)
初始化 \(\mathcal{A}\)（例如初始化神经网络）
初始化回放缓冲区 \(\mathcal{R}\)
对于 episode = 1, M 执行：
  采样一个目标 \(g\) 和一个初始状态 \(s_0\)。
  对于 t = 0, T-1 执行：
    使用来自 \(\mathcal{A}\) 的行为策略采样动作 \(a_t\)：\(a_t \leftarrow \pi_b(s_t || g)\)（|| 表示拼接）
    执行动作 \(a_t\) 并观测新状态 \(s_{t+1}\)
  结束 for
  对于 t = 0, T-1 执行：
    \(r_t := r(s_t, a_t, g)\)
    将转移 \(s_t||g, a_t, r_t, s_{t+1}||g)\ 存入 \(\mathcal{R}\)（标准经验回放）
    采样一组用于回放的额外目标 \(\mathcal{G} := \mathcal{S}(\text{当前回合})\)
    对于每个 \(g' \in \mathcal{G}\) 执行：
      \(r' := r(s_t, a_t, g')\)
      将转移 \(s_t||g', a_t, r', s_{t+1}||g')\ 存入 \(\mathcal{R}\)（HER）
    结束 for
  结束 for
  对于 t = 1, N 执行：
    从回放缓冲区 \(\mathcal{R}\) 采样一个小批量 \(\mathcal{B}\)
    使用 \(\mathcal{A}\) 和小批量 \(\mathcal{B}\) 执行一步优化
  结束 for
结束 for
HER可被视为一种隐式课程学习，因为用于回放的目标自然地由随机智能体也能轻易达成的简单目标向更困难的目标转变。然而，与显式课程不同，HER无需对初始环境状态的分布有任何控制。HER不仅能在极其稀疏的奖励下学习，在我们的实验中，它使用稀疏奖励时的表现也优于使用塑形奖励（见第4.4节）。这些结果说明了奖励塑形的实际挑战，并且塑形奖励往往会在我们真正关心的度量（如二元成功/失败）上做出妥协。

paras.en: The video presenting our experiments is available at https://goo.gl/SMrQnI. This section is organized as follows. In Sec. 4.1 we introduce multi-goal RL environments we use for the experiments as well as our training procedure. In Sec. 4.2 we compare the performance of DDPG with and without HER. In Sec. 4.3 we check if HER improves performance in the single-goal setup. In Sec. 4.4 we analyze the effects of using shaped reward functions. In Sec. 4.5 we compare different strategies for sampling additional goals for HER. In Sec. 4.6 we show the results of the experiments on the physical robot.
paras.zh: 展示我们实验的视频可在 https://goo.gl/SMrQnI 获取。本节组织如下。在第4.1节中，我们介绍实验中使用的多目标RL环境以及训练过程。在第4.2节中，我们比较有HER和无HER的DDPG性能。在第4.3节中，我们检查HER是否在单目标设置中提升性能。在第4.4节中，我们分析使用塑形奖励函数的效果。在第4.5节中，我们比较HER采样额外目标的不同策略。在第4.6节中，我们展示在物理机器人上的实验结果。

paras.en: There are no standard environments for multi-goal RL and therefore we created our own environments. We decided to use manipulation environments based on an existing hardware robot to ensure that the challenges we face correspond as closely as possible to the real world. In all experiments we use a 7-DOF Fetch Robotics arm which has a two-fingered parallel gripper. The robot is simulated using the MuJoCo (Todorov et al., 2012) physics engine. The whole training procedure is performed in the simulation but we show in Sec. 4.6 that the trained policies perform well on the physical robot without any fine-tuning.
paras.zh: 目前没有标准的多目标RL环境，因此我们创建了自己的环境。我们决定使用基于现有硬件机器人的操作环境，以确保我们面临的挑战尽可能贴近真实世界。在所有实验中，我们使用一个7自由度Fetch Robotics机械臂，配有双指平行夹爪。机器人使用MuJoCo（Todorov等人，2012）物理引擎进行仿真。整个训练过程在仿真中完成，但我们在第4.6节中展示了训练好的策略在物理机器人上无需任何微调即可表现良好。

paras.en: Observations: In this paragraph relative means relative to the current gripper position. The policy is given as input the absolute position of the gripper, the relative position of the object and the target, as well as the distance between the fingers. The Q-function is additionally given the linear velocity of the gripper and fingers as well as relative linear and angular velocity of the object. We decided to restrict the input to the policy in order to make deployment on the physical robot easier. Actions: None of the problems we consider require gripper rotation and therefore we keep it fixed. Action space is 4-dimensional. Three dimensions specify the desired relative gripper position at the next timestep. We use MuJoCo constraints to move the gripper towards the desired position but Jacobian-based control could be used instead. The last dimension specifies the desired distance between the 2 fingers which are position controlled. Strategy S for sampling goals for replay: Unless stated otherwise HER uses replay with the goal corresponding to the final state in each episode, i.e. S(s0, ..., sT) = m(sT). We compare different strategies for choosing which goals to replay with in Sec. 4.5. 4.2
paras.zh: 观察：在本段中，“相对”指的是相对于当前夹爪位置。策略的输入包括夹爪的绝对位置、物体和目标的相对位置，以及手指间的距离。Q函数额外接收夹爪和手指的线速度以及物体的相对线速度和角速度。我们决定限制策略的输入，以便于在物理机器人上的部署。动作：我们考虑的所有问题都不需要夹爪旋转，因此我们保持其固定。动作空间是四维的。三个维度指定下一时间步期望的相对夹爪位置。我们使用MuJoCo约束将夹爪移向期望位置，但也可以使用基于雅可比的控制。最后一个维度指定两根手指之间的期望距离，该距离由位置控制。用于重放的目标采样策略S：除非另有说明，HER使用的重放目标对应于每个回合的最终状态，即S(s0, ..., sT) = m(sT)。我们在第4.5节比较了不同选择重放目标的策略。4.2

paras.en: In order to verify if HER improves performance we evaluate DDPG with and without HER on all 3 tasks. Moreover, we compare against DDPG with count-based exploration (Strehl and Littman, 2005; Kolter and Ng, 2009; Tang et al., 2016; Bellemare et al., 2016; Ostrovski et al., 2017). For HER we store each transition in the replay buffer twice: once with the goal used for the generation of the episode and once with the goal corresponding to the final state from the episode (we call this strategy final). In Sec. 4.5 we perform ablation studies of different strategies S for choosing goals for replay, here we include the best version from Sec. 4.5 in the plot for comparison. DDPG
paras.zh: 为了验证HER是否能提升性能，我们在所有三个任务上评估了使用和不使用HER的DDPG。此外，我们与基于计数的探索（Strehl and Littman, 2005; Kolter and Ng, 2009; Tang et al., 2016; Bellemare et al., 2016; Ostrovski et al., 2017）的DDPG进行比较。对于HER，我们将每个转换存储到重放缓冲区两次：一次使用生成该回合的目标，一次使用对应于该回合最终状态的目标（我们将此策略称为final）。在第4.5节中，我们对选择重放目标的不同策略S进行了消融研究，此处我们在图中包含了第4.5节的最佳版本以进行比较。DDPG

paras.en: The target position is relative to the current object position. The successful deployment on a physical robot (Sec. 4.6) confirms that our control model produces movements which are reproducible on the physical robot despite not being fully physically plausible. We discretize the state space and use an intrinsic reward of the form \(α / √N\), where \α\ is a hyperparameter and \N\ is the number of times the given state was visited. The discretization works as follows: We take the relative position of the box and the target and then discretize every coordinate using a grid with a stepsize \β\ which is a hyperparameter. We have performed a hyperparameter search over \α ∈ {0.032, 0.064, 0.125, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32}\, \β ∈ {1cm, 2cm, 4cm, 8cm}\. The best results were obtained using \α = 1\ and \β = 1cm\ and these are the results we report. We also evaluated DQN (without HER) on our tasks and it was not able to solve any of them.
paras.zh: 目标位置相对于当前物体位置。在物理机器人上的成功部署（第4.6节）证实，尽管我们的控制模型并非完全物理上合理，但它产生的运动在物理机器人上是可以复现的。我们将状态空间离散化，并使用形式为\(α / √N\)的内在奖励，其中\α\是超参数，\N\是给定状态被访问的次数。离散化过程如下：我们取盒子和目标的相对位置，然后使用步长为\β\（超参数）的网格对每个坐标进行离散化。我们对\α ∈ {0.032, 0.064, 0.125, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32}\和\β ∈ {1cm, 2cm, 4cm, 8cm}\进行了超参数搜索。使用\α = 1\和\β = 1cm\得到最佳结果，这些就是我们所报告的结果。我们还评估了DQN（不含HER）在我们的任务上的表现，它无法解决任何任务。

paras.en: Does HER improve performance even if there is only one goal we care about?
paras.zh: 即使我们只关心一个目标，HER能否提升性能？

paras.en: In this section we evaluate whether HER improves performance in the case where there is only one goal we care about. To this end, we repeat the experiments from the previous section but the goal state is identical in all episodes. From Fig. 4 it is clear that DDPG+HER performs much better than pure DDPG even if the goal state is identical in all episodes. More importantly, comparing Fig. 3 and Fig. 4 we can also notice that HER learns faster if training episodes contain multiple goals, so in practice it is advisable to train on multiple goals even if we care only about one of them. 4.4
paras.zh: 在本节中，我们评估在只关心一个目标的情况下HER能否提升性能。为此，我们重复了上一节的实验，但目标状态在所有回合中都是相同的。从图4可以清楚地看出，即使目标状态在所有回合中相同，DDPG+HER也远优于纯DDPG。更重要的是，比较图3和图4，我们还可以注意到，如果训练回合包含多个目标，HER学习得更快，因此在实际应用中，即使我们只关心其中一个目标，也建议在多个目标上进行训练。4.4

paras.en: So far we only considered binary rewards of the form r(s, a, g) = -[|g - s_object| > ]. In this section we check how the performance of DDPG with and without HER changes if we replace this reward with one which is shaped. We considered reward functions of the form r(s, a, g) = ⟦⟦⟦|g - s_object|^p - |g - s'_object|^p, where s' is the state of the environment after the execution of the action a in the state s and ⟦⟦⟦{0, 1}, p ⟦⟦⟦{1, 2} are hyperparameters.
paras.zh: 到目前为止，我们只考虑了形式为 r(s, a, g) = -[|g - s_object| > ] 的二元奖励。在本节中，我们检查如果将这种奖励替换为成形奖励，DDPG 在有和没有 HER 的情况下的性能如何变化。我们考虑了形式为 r(s, a, g) = ⟦⟦⟦|g - s_object|^p - |g - s'_object|^p 的奖励函数，其中 s' 是在状态 s 中执行动作 a 后的环境状态，⟦⟦⟦{0, 1}, p ⟦⟦⟦{1, 2} 是超参数。

paras.en: The following two reasons can cause shaped rewards to perform so poorly: (1) There is a huge discrepancy between what we optimize (i.e. a shaped reward function) and the success condition (i.e. whether the object is within some radius from the goal at the end of the episode); (2) Shaped rewards penalize inappropriate behavior (e.g. moving the box in a wrong direction), which may hinder exploration. It can cause the agent to learn not to touch the box at all if it cannot manipulate it precisely, and we noticed such behavior in some of our experiments. Our results suggest that domain-agnostic reward shaping does not work well (at least in the simple forms we have tried). Of course, for every problem there exists a reward which makes it easy (Ng et al., 1999), but designing such shaped rewards requires a lot of domain knowledge and may in some cases not be much easier than directly scripting the policy. This strengthens our belief that learning from sparse, binary rewards is an important problem.
paras.zh: 成形奖励表现如此糟糕可能由以下两个原因造成：(1) 我们优化的目标（即成形奖励函数）与成功条件（即情节结束时物体是否在目标一定半径内）之间存在巨大差异；(2) 成形奖励惩罚了不当行为（例如，将盒子移向错误方向），这可能会阻碍探索。如果智能体无法精确操作物体，它可能导致智能体学会根本不触碰盒子，我们在某些实验中观察到了这种行为。我们的结果表明，与领域无关的奖励成形效果不佳（至少在我们尝试的简单形式中如此）。当然，对于每个问题，都存在使问题变得简单的奖励 (Ng et al., 1999)，但设计这样的成形奖励需要大量领域知识，并且在某些情况下并不比直接编写策略容易多少。这加强了我们的信念，即从稀疏二元奖励中学习是一个重要问题。

paras.en: How many goals should we replay each trajectory with and how to choose them?
paras.zh: 每个轨迹应该用多少个目标进行重放，以及如何选择这些目标？

paras.en: In this section we experimentally evaluate different strategies (i.e. S in Alg. 1) for choosing goals to use with HER. So far the only additional goals we used for replay were the ones corresponding to the states visited in the trajectory. We also tried to rescale the distances so that the range of rewards is similar to the case of binary rewards, clipping big distances and adding a simple (linear or quadratic) term encouraging the gripper to move towards the object, but none of these techniques led to successful training.
paras.zh: 在本节中，我们通过实验评估了用于 HER 的不同目标选择策略（即算法 1 中的 S）。到目前为止，我们用于重放的唯一额外目标是轨迹中访问过的状态对应的目标。我们还尝试重新缩放距离，使奖励范围与二元奖励的情况相似，裁剪大距离并添加一个简单的（线性或二次）项鼓励夹爪向物体移动，但这些技术都没有导致成功的训练。

paras.en: number of additional goals used to replay each transition with
paras.zh: 用于重放每个转移的额外目标数量

paras.en: We took a policy for the pick-and-place task trained in the simulator (version with the future strategy and k = 4 from Sec. 4.5) and deployed it on a physical fetch robot without any fine-tuning. The box position was predicted using a separately trained CNN using raw fetch head camera images. See Appendix B for details. Initially the policy succeeded in 2 out of 5 trials. It was not robust to small errors in the box position estimation because it was trained on perfect state coming from the simulation. After retraining the policy with Gaussian noise (std=1cm) added to observations, the success rate increased to 5/5. The video showing some of the trials is available at https://goo.gl/SMrQnI.
paras.zh: 我们将一个在模拟器中训练好的拾取-放置任务策略（采用未来策略且k=4的版本，见第4.5节）部署到真实的Fetch机器人上，未进行任何微调。盒子位置通过一个单独训练的CNN利用Fetch头部摄像头的原始图像进行预测。详见附录B。最初，该策略在5次试验中成功2次。由于它在模拟器提供的完美状态上训练，因此对盒子位置估计的小误差不够鲁棒。在观测中加入高斯噪声（标准差=1cm）重新训练策略后，成功率提升至5/5。展示部分试验的视频可见https://goo.gl/SMrQnI。

paras.en: The technique of experience replay has been introduced in Lin (1992) and became very popular after it was used in the DQN agent playing Atari (Mnih et al., 2015). Prioritized experience replay (Schaul et al., 2015b) is an improvement to experience replay which prioritizes transitions in the replay buffer in order to speed up training. It is orthogonal to our work and both approaches can be easily combined. Learning simultaneously policies for multiple tasks have been heavily explored in the context of policy search, e.g., Schmidhuber and Huber (1990); Caruana (1998); Da Silva et al. (2012); Kober et al. (2012); Devin et al. (2016); Pinto and Gupta (2016). Learning off-policy value functions for multiple tasks was investigated by Foster and Dayan (2002) and Sutton et al. (2011). Our work is most heavily based on Schaul et al. (2015a) who considers training a single neural network approximating multiple value functions. Learning simultaneously to perform multiple tasks has been also investigated for a long time in the context of Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning, e.g., Bakker and Schmidhuber (2004); Vezhnevets et al. (2017). Our approach may be seen as a form of implicit curriculum learning (Elman, 1993; Bengio et al., 2009). While curriculum is now often used for training neural networks (e.g., Zaremba and Sutskever (2014); Graves et al. (2016)), the curriculum is almost always hand-crafted. The problem of automatic curriculum generation was approached by Schmidhuber (2004) who constructed an asymptotically optimal algorithm for this problem using program search. Another interesting approach is PowerPlay (Schmidhuber, 2013; Srivastava et al., 2013) which is a general framework for automatic task selection. Graves et al. (2017) consider a setup where there is a fixed discrete set of tasks and empirically evaluate different strategies for automatic curriculum generation in this setting. Another approach investigated by Sukhbaatar et al. (2017) and Held et al. (2017) uses self-play between the policy and a task-setter in order to automatically generate goal states which are on the border of what the current policy can achieve. Our approach is orthogonal to these techniques and can be combined with them. We have also tried replaying the goals which are close to the ones achieved in the near future but it has not performed better than the future strategy. The Q-function approximator was trained using exact observations. It does not have to be robust to noisy observations because it is not used during the deployment on the physical robot.
paras.zh: 经验回放技术由Lin（1992）引入，并在用于玩Atari游戏的DQN智能体（Mnih等人，2015）后变得非常流行。优先经验回放（Schaul等人，2015b）是对经验回放的一种改进，它对回放缓冲区中的转移赋予优先级以加速训练。它与我们的工作正交，两种方法可以轻松结合。多任务策略的同步学习在策略搜索领域已被广泛探索，例如Schmidhuber和Huber（1990）；Caruana（1998）；Da Silva等人（2012）；Kober等人（2012）；Devin等人（2016）；Pinto和Gupta（2016）。Foster和Dayan（2002）以及Sutton等人（2011）研究了多任务的离策略价值函数学习。我们的工作主要基于Schaul等人（2015a），他们考虑训练一个单一的神经网络来近似多个价值函数。在分层强化学习背景下，同时学习执行多个任务也已被研究了很长时间，例如Bakker和Schmidhuber（2004）；Vezhnevets等人（2017）。我们的方法可视为一种隐式课程学习（Elman，1993；Bengio等人，2009）。虽然课程学习现在常用于训练神经网络（例如Zaremba和Sutskever（2014）；Graves等人（2016）），但课程几乎总是手工设计的。自动课程生成问题由Schmidhuber（2004）提出，他使用程序搜索构建了一个渐进最优算法。另一种有趣的方法是PowerPlay（Schmidhuber，2013；Srivastava等人，2013），它是一个用于自动任务选择的通用框架。Graves等人（2017）考虑了一个固定离散任务集的设置，并在此设置下经验评估了不同的自动课程生成策略。Sukhbaatar等人（2017）和Held等人（2017）研究的另一种方法使用策略和任务设置者之间的自我对弈，以自动生成位于当前策略能力边界上的目标状态。我们的方法与这些技术正交，并可以与它们结合。我们还尝试了重放与近期实现目标接近的目标，但效果并不优于未来策略。Q函数近似器使用精确观测进行训练，它不需要对噪声观测鲁棒，因为在物理机器人部署时不使用它。

paras.en: We introduced a novel technique called Hindsight Experience Replay which makes possible applying RL algorithms to problems with sparse and binary rewards. Our technique can be combined with an arbitrary off-policy RL algorithm and we experimentally demonstrated that with DQN and DDPG. We showed that HER allows training policies which push, slide and pick-and-place objects with a robotic arm to the specified positions while the vanilla RL algorithm fails to solve these tasks. We also showed that the policy for the pick-and-place task performs well on the physical robot without any fine-tuning. As far as we know, it is the first time so complicated behaviors were learned using only sparse, binary rewards. We would also like to thank Rein Houthooft and the whole OpenAI team for fruitful discussions as well as Bowen Baker for performing some additional experiments.
paras.zh: 我们提出了一种名为后见经验回放的新技术，使得将强化学习算法应用于稀疏和二元奖励问题成为可能。我们的技术可以与任意离策略强化学习算法结合，并通过DQN和DDPG进行了实验验证。我们表明，HER可以训练策略使机器人臂将物体推、滑动和拾取-放置到指定位置，而原始的强化学习算法无法解决这些任务。我们还展示了拾取-放置任务的策略在物理机器人上表现良好，无需任何微调。据我们所知，这是首次仅使用稀疏、二元奖励学习如此复杂的行为。致谢：感谢Ankur Handa、Jonathan Ho、John Schulman、Matthias Plappert、Tim Salimans和Vikash Kumar对本文先前版本的反馈。我们还感谢Rein Houthooft和整个OpenAI团队富有成果的讨论，以及Bowen Baker进行的一些额外实验。

paras.en: In this section we provide more details on our experimental setup and hyperparameters used. Bit-flipping experiment: We used a network with 1 hidden layer with 256 neurons. The length of each episode was equal to the number of bits and the episode was considered successful if the goal state was achieved at an arbitrary timestep during the episode. All other hyperparameters used were the same as in the case of DDPG experiments. State-goal distributions: For all tasks the initial position of the gripper is fixed, for the pushing and sliding tasks it is located just above the table surface and for pushing it is located 20 cm above the table. The object is placed randomly on the table in the 30 cm x 30 cm (20 cm x 20 cm for sliding) square with the center directly under the gripper (both objects are 5 cm wide). For pushing, the goal state is sampled uniformly from the same square as the box position. In the pick-and-place task the target is located in the air in order to force the robot to grasp (and not just push). The x and y coordinates of the goal position are sampled uniformly from the mentioned square and the height is sampled uniformly between 10 cm and 45 cm. For sliding the goal position is sampled from a 60 cm x 60 cm square centered 40 cm away from the initial gripper position. For all tasks we discard initial state-goal pairs in which the goal is already satisfied. Network architecture: Both actor and critic networks have 3 hidden layers with 64 hidden units in each layer. Hidden layers use ReLU activation function and the actor output layer uses tanh. The output of the tanh is then rescaled so that it lies in the range \([-5\text{cm}, 5\text{cm}]\). In order to prevent tanh saturation and vanishing gradients we add the square of the their preactivations to the actor's cost function. Training procedure: We train for 200 epochs. Each epoch consists of 50 cycles where each cycle consists of running the policy for 16 episodes and then performing 40 optimization steps on minibatches of size 128 sampled uniformly from a replay buffer consisting of \(10^6\) transitions. We update the target networks after every cycle using the decay coefficient of 0.95. Apart from using the target network for computing Q-targets for the critic we also use it in testing episodes as it is more stable than the main network. The whole training procedure is distributed over 8 threads. For the Adam optimization algorithm we use the learning rate of 0.001 and the default values from Tensorflow framework (Abadi et al., 2016) for the other hyperparameters. We use the discount factor of \(\gamma = 0.98\) for all transitions including the ones ending an episode. Moreover, we clip the targets used to train the critic to the range of possible values, i.e. \([ -\frac{1}{1-\gamma}, 0 ]\). Input scaling: Neural networks have problems dealing with inputs of different magnitudes and therefore it is crucial to scale them properly. To this end, we rescale inputs to neural networks so that they have mean zero and standard deviation equal to one and then clip them to the range \([-5, 5]\). Means and standard deviations used for rescaling are computed using all the observations encountered so far in the training. Exploration: The behavioral policy we use for exploration works as follows. With probability 20% we sample (uniformly) a random action from the hypercube of valid actions. Otherwise, we take the output of the policy network and add independently to every coordinate normal noise with standard deviation equal to 5% of the total range of allowed values on this coordinate. Simulation: Every episode consists of 50 environment timesteps, each of which consists of 10 MuJoCo steps with \(\Delta t = 0.002\text{s}\). MuJoCo uses soft constraints for contacts and therefore object penetration is possible. It can be minimized by using a small timestep and more constraint solver epochs but it would slow down the simulation. We encountered some penetration in the pushing task (the agent learnt to push the box into the table in a way that it is pushed out by contact forces onto the target). In order to avoid this behaviour we added to the reward a term penalizing the squared depth of penetration for every contact pair. 14
paras.zh: 在本节中，我们提供了实验设置和超参数的更多细节。翻转位实验：我们使用了一个具有1个隐藏层（256个神经元）的网络。每个回合的长度等于位数，如果在回合中的任意时间步达到目标状态，则认为该回合成功。所有其他使用的超参数与DDPG实验相同。状态-目标分布：对于所有任务，夹爪的初始位置是固定的，对于推和滑动任务，它位于桌面正上方，对于推任务，它位于桌面上方20厘米处。物体被随机放置在桌面上30厘米×30厘米（滑动任务为20厘米×20厘米）的正方形内，中心正对夹爪下方（两个物体宽5厘米）。对于推任务，目标状态从与盒子位置相同的正方形中均匀采样。在拾取和放置任务中，目标位于空中，以迫使机器人抓取（而不仅仅是推）。目标位置的x和y坐标从所述正方形中均匀采样，高度在10厘米到45厘米之间均匀采样。对于滑动任务，目标位置从一个60厘米×60厘米的正方形中采样，该正方形中心距离初始夹爪位置40厘米。对于所有任务，我们丢弃初始状态-目标对中目标已经满足的情况。网络架构：演员和评论家网络都有3个隐藏层，每层64个隐藏单元。隐藏层使用ReLU激活函数，演员输出层使用tanh。tanh的输出然后被重新缩放，使其位于\([-5\text{cm}, 5\text{cm}]\)范围内。为了防止tanh饱和和梯度消失，我们将预激活的平方添加到演员的成本函数中。训练过程：我们训练200个周期。每个周期由50个循环组成，每个循环包括运行策略16个回合，然后对从包含\(10^6\)个转移的回放缓冲区中均匀采样的128大小的迷你批次执行40个优化步骤。我们在每个循环后使用衰减系数0.95更新目标网络。除了使用目标网络计算评论家的Q目标外，我们还在测试回合中使用它，因为它比主网络更稳定。整个训练过程分布在8个线程上。对于Adam优化算法，我们使用学习率0.001和Tensorflow框架(Abadi et al., 2016)的其他超参数默认值。我们对所有转移（包括结束一个回合的转移）使用折扣因子\(\gamma = 0.98\)。此外，我们将用于训练评论家的目标裁剪到可能值的范围内，即\([ -\frac{1}{1-\gamma}, 0 ]\)。输入缩放：神经网络在处理不同数量级的输入时存在问题，因此适当缩放输入至关重要。为此，我们重新缩放神经网络的输入，使其均值为零，标准差为一，然后将其裁剪到范围\([-5, 5]\)。用于重新缩放的均值和标准差使用训练中迄今为止遇到的所有观测值计算。探索：我们用于探索的行为策略如下。有20%的概率，我们从有效动作的超立方体中均匀采样一个随机动作。否则，我们取策略网络的输出，并在每个坐标上独立添加正态噪声，其标准差等于该坐标允许值总范围的5%。仿真：每个回合包含50个环境时间步，每个时间步包含10个MuJoCo步，其中\(\Delta t = 0.002\text{s}\)。MuJoCo对接触使用软约束，因此物体穿透是可能的。通过使用小时间步长和更多的约束求解器迭代可以最小化穿透，但这会减慢仿真速度。我们在推任务中遇到了一些穿透（智能体学会了将盒子推入桌子，使得接触力将盒子推出到目标上）。为了避免这种行为，我们在奖励中添加了一个惩罚每个接触对穿透深度平方的项。14

paras.en: Training time: Training for 200 epochs took us approximately 2.5 h for pushing and the pick-and-place tasks and 6 h for sliding (because physics simulation was slower for this task) using 8 CPU cores.
paras.zh: 训练时间：使用8个CPU核心，训练200个周期在推和拾取放置任务上大约需要2.5小时，在滑动任务上需要6小时（因为该任务的物理仿真较慢）。

paras.en: We have trained a convolutional neural network (CNN) which predicts the box position given the raw image from the fetch head camera. The CNN was trained using only images coming from the MuJoCo renderer. Despite the fact that training images were not photorealistic, the trained network performs well on real world data thanks to a high degree of randomization of textures, lightning and other visual parameters in training. This approach called domain randomization is described in more detail in Tobin et al. (2017). At the beginning of each episode we initialize a simulated environment using the box position predicted by the CNN and robot state coming from the physical robot. From this point we run the policy in the simulator. After each timestep we send the simulated robot joint angles to the real one which is position-controlled and uses the simulated data as targets.
paras.zh: 我们训练了一个卷积神经网络（CNN），它根据来自抓取头摄像头的原始图像预测盒子位置。该CNN仅使用来自MuJoCo渲染器的图像进行训练。尽管训练图像不是照片级真实的，但由于训练中纹理、光照和其他视觉参数的高度随机化，训练后的网络在真实世界数据上表现良好。这种方法称为域随机化，在Tobin等人(2017)中有更详细的描述。在每个回合开始时，我们使用CNN预测的盒子位置和来自物理机器人的机器人状态初始化一个仿真环境。从这一点开始，我们在仿真器中运行策略。在每个时间步后，我们将仿真的机器人关节角度发送给真实机器人，真实机器人采用位置控制，并使用仿真数据作为目标。
